sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “Charles-Louis Pothier.” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Author, born at Bordeaux on 18 April 1881, died at Clichy on 3 November 1962; elected full member of SACEM on 17 February 1912; Prix Trebitsch, 1943; Prix Albert Willemetz, 1947; Prix Centenaire, 1950; Prix Célestin Joubert, 1956; Grand Prix de la Chanson, 1958.
sources.title: Charles-Louis Pothier
sources.researchNote: The list of society prizes, running from 1943 to 1958, documents a standing in the profession that the catalogue records do not show, and the register confirms the places of birth and death.

media.title: Charles-Louis Pothier — portrait, Flossie programme, 1929
media.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of Charles-Louis Pothier in a suit and tie.
media.publicCaption: Charles-Louis Pothier, the Bordeaux-born lyricist who worked with René Pujol as librettist-parolier to Albert Willemetz at the Bouffes-Parisiens, in the author’s portrait from the programme of Flossie.
media.publicCreditLine: Pierre Carles; programme of Flossie, Bouffes-Parisiens, 1929, collection Jacques Gana, via the Encyclopédie de la comédie musicale.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The photograph is credited to Pierre Carles, but the photographer could not be traced: he holds no authority record or Wikidata item, appears in no Wikimedia Commons attribution, and is absent as a creator from the digitised holdings of the Bibliothèque nationale de France. Without a date of death the French term cannot be computed, and a French work published in 1929 would in any case have had United States copyright restored by the URAA if it was still protected in France in 1996. The site reproducing the programme grants no licence, stating that illustrations remain the copyright of their respective rightsholders. A reduced-resolution reproduction (700 × 594 px) is used here for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper collaborator.
